findings.title: Reject reserved keywords in declaration/call binding positions
findings.requirement: Unsupported source must remain UNKNOWN and must not register/request sample APIs or yield available/known-empty content.
findings.input: reserved-getter-invalid.js: otherwise matching narrow native fetch module, with function frameRead renamed to reserved keyword if and caller await if(b,n).
findings.independent_syntax_evidence: Node --check exits1: SyntaxError Unexpected token if. Valid paired source exits0. Neither file executed as JS.
findings.actual: Actual new collect accepts binding_proof.complete=true, CURRENT_CODE_CONFIRMED; registers sample3; makes11 synthetic business GETs and yields question/choice/answer AVAILABLE; outcome READONLY_REVIEW.
findings.cause: lex classifies any identifier-shaped word as id; functions and call_chain accept kind=id for function/parameter/local/call names, without binding-position reserved-word validation.
findings.expected: Invalid/out-of-supported-grammar source stays UNKNOWN; only six fixed GETs, zero sample registration/GET, no AVAILABLE/KNOWN_EMPTY sample.
findings.correction_scope: Validate legal supported JS binding identifiers/grammar; reject invalid reserved words. This does not require supporting more JS forms or executing script code.
findings.limits: Synthetic transport/UI/original/file boundaries; actual new parser/current_code/register_sample/collect/frame/content binding used. Current frontend applicability and real platform behavior remain unproved.
